From adbe6991efd36104ac9eaf751993d35eaa7f493a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Bjorn Helgaas <bhelgaas@google.com>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2013 16:29:55 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] bio-integrity: Fix use of bs->bio_integrity_pool after free

This fixes a copy and paste error introduced by 9f060e2231
("block: Convert integrity to bvec_alloc_bs()").

Found by Coverity (CID 1020654).

Signed-off-by: Bjorn Helgaas <bhelgaas@google.com>
Acked-by: Kent Overstreet <koverstreet@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

diff --git a/fs/bio-integrity.c b/fs/bio-integrity.c
index 8fb42916d8a2..45e944fe52a6 100644
--- a/fs/bio-integrity.c
+++ b/fs/bio-integrity.c
@@ -734,7 +734,7 @@ void bioset_integrity_free(struct bio_set *bs)
 		mempool_destroy(bs->bio_integrity_pool);
 
 	if (bs->bvec_integrity_pool)
-		mempool_destroy(bs->bio_integrity_pool);
+		mempool_destroy(bs->bvec_integrity_pool);
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL(bioset_integrity_free);
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `fs/bio-integrity.c`**
   - The line that previously destroyed the `bio_integrity_pool` when `bvec_integrity_pool` was not null has been modified. 
   - The incorrect line:
     ```c
     mempool_destroy(bs->bio_integrity_pool);
     ```
   - Has been replaced with the correct line:
     ```c
     mempool_destroy(bs->bvec_integrity_pool);
     ```

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `fs/bio-integrity.c` addresses a bug that was introduced in a previous commit. The change corrects a copy-and-paste error where the wrong memory pool (`bio_integrity_pool`) was being destroyed instead of the intended `bvec_integrity_pool`. This fix ensures that the correct resources are released, preventing potential use-after-free errors and improving the stability of the code. The patch was identified through static analysis (Coverity) and is part of ongoing maintenance to ensure code correctness.

Here is the commit message:
bio-integrity: Fix use of bs->bio_integrity_pool after free

This fixes a copy and paste error introduced by 9f060e2231
("block: Convert integrity to bvec_alloc_bs()").

Found by Coverity (CID 1020654).

Signed-off-by: Bjorn Helgaas <bhelgaas@google.com>
Acked-by: Kent Overstreet <koverstreet@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by a copy-and-paste error in the code where the wrong memory pool (`bio_integrity_pool`) was being destroyed instead of the intended `bvec_integrity_pool`. This could lead to a use-after-free situation, where the program attempts to access memory that has already been freed, potentially causing crashes or undefined behavior.

Here is the patch:
 
 void bioset_integrity_free(struct bio_set *bs)
 {
 	if (bs->bio_integrity_pool)
 		mempool_destroy(bs->bio_integrity_pool);
 
 	if (bs->bvec_integrity_pool)
-		mempool_destroy(bs->bio_integrity_pool);
+		mempool_destroy(bs->bvec_integrity_pool);
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL(bioset_integrity_free);

Reason:
The bug occurs because of a copy-and-paste error where `bs->bio_integrity_pool` was incorrectly used in the `mempool_destroy` function instead of the intended `bs->bvec_integrity_pool`. This leads to a use-after-free situation, as accessing the `bio_integrity_pool` after it has been freed can result in crashes or undefined behavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
mempool_destroy(bs->bvec_integrity_pool);
```
Reason:
The fix correctly changes the call to `mempool_destroy` to use `bs->bvec_integrity_pool`, which is the intended memory pool that should be destroyed. This ensures that the program does not attempt to free or access memory that has already been freed, thus preventing the use-after-free issue.
